prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
S068: Manual override is permitted for chemical feed, valve sequencing, and filter start or stop actions only when automatic control is unavailable or inappropriate for the condition.
S069: An operator placing equipment in manual control is expected to state the reason, monitor the affected process variable closely, and restore automatic control as soon as practicable.
S070: Manual chemical feed changes are made in small increments unless an immediate water-quality risk requires a larger correction approved by the Chief Operator.
S071: If analyzer feedback is lost, operating staff hold the last verified safe dose or revert to an approved fixed dose while collecting additional grab samples.
S072: A sustained loss of coagulation effectiveness is treated as a process deviation and prompts review of chemical strength, feed pump status, mixing energy, and raw-water characteristics.
S073: The Chlorine Contact Basin is considered in the response because excessive particulate carryover can affect downstream disinfectant demand and contact performance.
S074: The Clearwell Level Controller remains coordinated with filter production so that filter shutdowns, backwashes, and return-to-service decisions do not create avoidable storage swings.
S075: When filter capacity is reduced, the Distribution Dispatcher is advised of expected production limits before changes affect the High Service Pump Header.
S076: After any significant deviation, the Chief Operator reviews trends from the affected operating period and confirms that corrective actions restored stable clarified and filtered water quality.
S077: Following operating deviations, laboratory sampling provides independent confirmation that treatment targets have returned to acceptable control ranges.
S078: The Chief Operator establishes daily sampling priorities based on plant conditions, regulatory monitoring requirements, and recent process adjustments.
S079: The Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench is also known as Sparrow for local bench labeling during sample receipt.
S080: Field samples are labeled at collection with location, time, collector initials, preservation method, and requested analyses before they leave operating areas.
S081: The Laboratory Technician checks container type, holding time, temperature, preservative status, and seal condition before logging a sample for analysis.
S082: Samples from the River Intake Pump Station, Raw Water Screen Channel, North Filter Gallery, South Filter Gallery, Chlorine Contact Basin, and High Service Pump Header are verified against the current sampling schedule before testing begins.
S083: The Laboratory Technician uses the Alum Batch Ticket to verify chemical lot identity before recording related laboratory observations.
S084: The Laboratory Technician prepares and sends the Sample Chain Slip after verifying that custody entries are complete and legible.
S085: The Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench sends the Jar Test Photograph Set after the comparison images have been checked for date, time, and sample identifiers.
S086: Lantern must retain accepted laboratory result timestamps with the associated process trend interval so that reconciliation can be repeated during audits.
S087: Field meter readings used for immediate control are treated as provisional until they are compared with laboratory results collected from the same location and time window.
S088: The Laboratory Technician records any mismatch between bottle labels, bench log entries, and operator notes before assigning an acceptance status to the sample.
S089: If a sample is received outside the approved holding time or temperature range, the result may be used for troubleshooting but is not accepted for compliance reporting.
S090: Calibration checks, method blanks, duplicate measurements, and control standards are reviewed before process measurements are released to operations.
S091: Results associated with failed quality checks are flagged, investigated, and either corrected with documented justification or rejected from the accepted data set.
S092: The Duty Engineer reviews significant differences between field readings and laboratory values when those differences could affect chemical feed, filter loading, or disinfection decisions.
S093: For turbidity and particle-related analyses, the Laboratory Technician confirms that sample mixing, settling time, and instrument range are appropriate for the expected raw or filtered water condition.
S094: For disinfectant residual analyses, the Laboratory Technician confirms reagent condition, sample contact time, and measurement timing before accepting the result.
S095: When a Chlorine Residual Alarm is active, related grab samples receive priority handling so that alarm response can be checked against an independent measurement.
S096: The Chief Operator is notified when laboratory confirmation does not support the field indication that caused an operating adjustment.
S097: Accepted laboratory results are reconciled to operating trends by matching collection time, sample point, process state, and recent manual observations.
S098: If Storm Intake Mode changes the character of incoming water, the sampling frequency is increased until raw and settled water measurements show stable behavior.
S099: The Backwash Recovery Tank is sampled after return-to-process events when recovered water quality could influence filter performance or finished water stability.
S100: The Laboratory Technician preserves all custody and acceptance records for review by the Chief Operator, Duty Engineer, and regulatory auditors.
S101: Planned maintenance is controlled through a work order process that ties each task to an approved operating window, a named responsible person, and a defined return-to-service condition.
S102: The Chief Operator reviews the next-day schedule with operations staff so that treatment capacity, water quality risk, and distribution demand are understood before work is released.
